newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cambridge says no decision on diamond plan.
newsitem.headline: Cambridge says no decision on diamond plan.

text.p: Marine exploration group Cambridge Gulf Exploration NL said on Tuesday it has made no decision on whether to abandon a bid to operate an offshore diamond mine.

Cambridge Gulf was responding an article in the West Australian newspaper on Tuesday which said it had abandoned a four-year effort to operate a diamond mine in favour of investing in a resource project that would provide immediate returns.
Trading in Cambridge shares on the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) were voluntarily halted before the start of trading on Tuesday pending the company's response to the article.
"Nothing could be further from the truth and Cambridge Gulf Exploration NL (CGE) has made no such decision," the company told the ASX.
"The directors recognise that any change in the direction or activities of the company will require shareholder approval," Cambridge said.

"CGE is committed to continuing the development of the marine diamond programme in the Joseph Bonaparte Gulf, where the cost of its investment to date, excluding capital assets, is in excess of A$29 million," the company said.

Laboratory analysis is proceeding on materials recovered in a drilling programme between December 1996 and April 1997 and the 200 samples and 32 vibrocores recovered in a supplementary shallow water programme, completed last week, the company said.

"The programmes have progressed the geological understanding of the prospective leases but, as previously reported, the company has experienced difficulties in completing the target quantities of bulk sampling holes," Cambridge said.

"In this regard, the company recognises that a different drilling technology is likely to be required in future, and the company officers will participate in demonstrations during June of alternative methods, not dependent upon drill string alignment," it said.
Cambridge also said Robert Draper was appointed board chairman on Tuesday.
